summary.intent: Verify the 0.17.0 release and the #425 merge, clean up local and remote state, push checkpoints, then work through the unblocked next items: re-run spec-drift checks across the five specs and fix what they found, plus the E165 hint.
summary.outcome: callisto 0.17.0 was released and #425 merged. Five parallel agents checked the specs, and one commit on branch fix/spec-drift-2026-11 fixed the code drift, corrected the spec text, hardened the release-PR script and added changesets. The commit was made but not pushed, and the trail closing, the OIDC decisions and the VER-GRP-06 call remain open.

repo: Entire auto-pushes checkpoints, so `entire checkpoint list --outgoing` showed nothing waiting.
The tool's own `status --check` validates changesets before commit; user-visible fixes in the crates need a `.changeset/*.md` file.

runner.rs filters environment per tool but passes the OIDC variables to npm, pnpm, yarn and bun. run-release.sh writes the temporary npm config's NPM_TOKEN line only when the token is non-empty, so OIDC trusted publishing is not blocked.
The #290 guard gaps are already closed: version_commit.rs now compares tree content and the git log has no 100-commit cap.
Spec-drift rates fell from about 14% in the 2026-10-20 review to roughly 8% (20 of 253 criteria) in this run. Most drift was wrong spec text rather than code bugs.
The subagents ran the prebuilt target/debug/callisto (built 13:13) against throwaway git fixtures. Targeted `cargo test --lib` runs were done one at a time so that binary was not replaced.
Calls to external systems such as closing Entire trails are blocked by the permission classifier, so they must be left to the user or explicitly allowed.

code.finding: `visible_only` rebuilds commands with `Command::new`, which drops `disable_help_subcommand`, so generated completions offered a `help` subcommand the CLI rejects (CLI-SURF-06).
`render_init` never rendered `report.diagnostics`, so the `changesets-config-key-dropped` warnings appeared only in JSON output (CLI-INIT-14).

The discovery walk reads the root package.json raw, so a leading BOM makes `npm_declares_private` fail to parse and a private, versionless root is listed as a package (E013). Membership reading strips the BOM at locate/membership.rs:10-21.

`write_version` deliberately writes an inherited version into the member's own [package] rather than [workspace.package], to avoid changing every other member. Only dependency spec rewrites go to the workspace manifest.

The fixed-group regression check compares only against the released member's base (alignment base at groups.rs:132-143), so an untagged member can silently move backwards, e.g. 2.7.3 to 1.4.1 (VER-GRP-06). VER-GRP-01 contradicts VER-GRP-06 here.
The E114 and E115 messages hardcoded `.changeset/pre.json`, ignoring a custom `[changesets] dir`. E115 was given a path field passed at three call sites (two in version.rs, one in release_pr.rs).

A colon-form package name in a changeset makes plain `status` fail with E316 and exit 1 instead of emitting the InvalidPackageName diagnostic. status_version_selector_tests.rs:195-212 asserts this, so it is intentional and the spec was changed.

workflow: Splitting the read-only spec-drift investigation across one parallel agent per spec worked well. Hand-backs are model output, so each was summarized and the fixes sorted into code bugs versus spec corrections.
Collecting all drift reports before fixing allowed a single PR and a consistent split between code and spec corrections.
Use `/usr/bin/git`, `python3 -I`, `shellcheck`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` as final gates before committing.

friction: The permission classifier blocked bulk-closing the 15 Entire trails because it counts as an external write.
The agents could not confirm which checkout built target/debug/callisto, so their runtime evidence was strong but not final.
The sandbox blocks github.com, so a successful workflow write in `init` could not be run live.
The spec-drift agents' counts and the transcript's tallies were inconsistent (e.g. workspace.json has 39 criteria, not 44), so totals needed care.
Several worktrees and branches could not be cleaned up without the user's say-so.
open_items: Close the 15 merged callisto trails (#129, #139, #141-#148, #151, #152, #159, #160, #163) and #162 once the hold workflow's draft-and-restore path has run.
Decide VER-GRP-06: raise E207 against every member's on-disk version (code) or document that untagged members may move back to the released member's line (spec).

OIDC trusted publishing needs the user's decisions on the config shape (callisto.toml switch versus generated-workflow option) and on whether Callisto's own release workflow may hold `id-token: write` on `execute`.
Fix the private workspace root listed as a package; needs the user's choice of exclusion shape.
Add the missing test assertions: MX-OUT-02, MX-ERR-06, MX-ERR-07, MX-DISC-02, WS-ID-08 (E101), WS-ID-09 (E007) and VER-CS-03 (BOM and lone CR).
Push the fix/spec-drift-2026-11 commit, open its PR and wait for CI. The release.json agent's report had not arrived when the spec corrections were applied.
Leave for the user: the `smoke-main`, `wf_cd627354`, `callisto-homebrew-tap` and `entire-hooks-update` worktrees and the `stack/docs-v1` branch.
Investigate the unexplained `uses: $/.github/...` lines in the workflows.
Optional: bisect the 20 ms slowdown at 400 packages.
Verify the new Hold release PR workflow's draft-and-restore path on the next release PR refresh.
